name: Electric-Assist Bicycle
description: A single category, not the three-class system: a low-speed electrically assisted bicycle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts that assists only while the rider pedals, to a top motor-powered speed under 20 mph. Defined by South Carolina Code §56-1-10(29), added by Act 114 of 2020, which also calls it a bicycle with a helper motor, and regulated as a bicycle by §56-5-3520.
restrictions: Two or three wheels, fully operable pedals, and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts (one horsepower)
Top motor-powered speed under 20 mph, measured with a 170-pound rider on a paved level surface
No throttle: the motor must disengage when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
No class system: South Carolina has not adopted the three-class model law
Manufacturers and distributors must permanently label it with its wattage and top assisted speed; owners may not remove or tamper with the label
Anyone who modifies it to change its speed must replace the label to match
No statewide minimum age or helmet requirement
Carries only as many riders as it's designed and equipped for
Treated as a bicycle, not a moped: no driver's license, registration or insurance
Rides by the same rules as a bicycle, including using an adjacent bicycle lane where one is provided
One whose motor exceeds 750 W, up to 1,500 W, is a moped, which needs a driver's or moped license and registration
